newsitem.title: USA: Pacificorp seeking ways to reduce costs.
newsitem.headline: Pacificorp seeking ways to reduce costs.

text.p: Pacificorp President and Chief Executive Officer Fred Buckman said higher non-operational costs are putting pressure on earnings from its domestic electric operations.
He said Pacificorp continues to search for additional ways to reduce costs in the domestic electric business in order to meet its earnings growth expectations for 1997.
Additionally, the company noted that in the second quarter of 1997, it recorded break-even results on its equity investment in the Hazelwood power station.

Hazelwood sells its generation output through a statewide generation pool and under bilateral contracts directly to Victorian distribution companies. Pool and contract prices vary depending on certain conditions, including weather, economic growth and other factors influencing supply and demand for electric power.

Power prices are highest in the Australian winter months because demand is highest, which generally is expected to result in higher profit margins for Hazelwood during the second and third calendar quarters.
